title: UserInfoResponse
description: A userinfo response, derived from identity_oidc::response::UserInfoResponse. An unsigned JSON document, not a JWT: the access token is already the authentication of this call, and the claims here are about the user the token was issued for. Every claim except sub carries skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", so a minimal response is exactly {"sub": "..."} — the four optional claims are ABSENT, never null.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; no route emits it in the bootstrap phase

sub.description: The subject. Always the same string for the same user, across every client — the discovery document advertises subject_types_supported == ["public"] and never "pairwise". UserInfoResponse::SUBJECT_CLAIM is this name.

name.description: The display name, present when the 'profile' scope was granted. Absent otherwise.
name.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the body, not null.

preferred_username.description: The preferred username, present when the 'profile' scope was granted. Absent otherwise.
preferred_username.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the body, not null.

email.description: The email address, present when the 'email' scope was granted. Absent otherwise.
email.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the body, not null.

email_verified.description: Whether the address has been proven. The field is not optional in spirit when email is present: UserInfoResponse::email_is_safely_usable is true only when email.is_some() AND email_verified == Some(true), and a client keying on email alone has an account-takeover bug. RFC 8414 marks this claim optional; this provider refuses to emit the pair unless both are meaningful.
email_verified.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] — absent from the body, not null. Absent alongside an email, the address is NOT safely usable.

x-omission-rule.rule: name, preferred_username, email and email_verified are omitted when None; sub is always present.
x-omission-rule.test: identity_oidc::response::tests::absent_claims_are_omitted_rather_than_serialised_as_null asserts the minimal body is exactly {"sub":"s"}
